articleTitle: Design and Realisation of the Simulation Model of the Stewart Platform using the MATLAB-Simulink and the Simscape Multibody Library
abstract: The paper deals with the derivation, realisation, and use of the simulation model of the Stewart platform using the simulation programme MATLAB-Simulink and the Simscape Multibody library. The creation of the simulation model of the parallel mechanism in the Simscape Multibody library using the imported data from the CAD software is presented in the paper. The presented simulation model allows the dynamic simulation of the platform for the desired change of the position and can be used for the optimization of the kinematic structure, actuators dimensioning, control design, and investigation of the workspace of the designed Stewart platform.

articleTitle: Combining a PI Controller with an Adaptive Feedforward Control in PMSM
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive feedforward control combined with a PI controller to be applied to a Permanent Magnetic Synchronous Machine (PMSM). The adaptive technique is realized by using an Extended Kalman Filter which provides for the estimate of paramteres and states necessary for the adaption. The estimated inductivities and the estimated speed are used in a feedforward control to improve the reference variable attitude. The impact of the feedforward control on the control will be examined and the PI controller will be set up.

articleTitle: Smart Meter in Voltage Control System of Power Network
abstract: The use of microgeneration in low-voltage (LV) power networks based on prosumer solar installations (PV) has brought many benefits. Larger scale power generation can also have undesirable effects - including dynamic voltage changes that exceed limits. The paper presents a model of communication channel for remote data reading from a 3-phase energy meter in terms of using the meter as a sensor in the voltage control system in the low-voltage power network. The model uses the LoRaWAN network based on the LoriotOR cloud platform and the developed DLMS protocol converter to the LoRa protocol, which as an end node connected to the meter interface. The test results of the developed smart meter in voltage control system of power network are presented in the article.

articleTitle: A ROS-based Control Application for a Robotic Platform Using the Gazebo 3D Simulator
abstract: This paper presents a ROS-based control application for a robotic platform, using the Gazebo 3D simulator that will allow a user to see and understand the simulation and moving of a mobile robot through a predefined map before being used in the real world. Usually, developers in the field of robotics need to test, verify and validate the dynamics of the robot in specific environments. Nowadays, the availability of virtual tools allows developers to create virtual working environments, and to do a targeted simulation of robots' dynamics. This approach highly reduces the times necessary for preparing the robot-specific content (design, deployment, environment), and afterwards the robot dynamics debugging. In our paper, we will detail these steps while considering the particulars of the mobile robot that is under development. For this, we created a replica of our robot simulated in Gazebo, a map of the robot's working environment, and, we have provided support for the robot's main applications: navigation, exploration, and interaction with sensors. All these elements are essential to simulate and visualize the robot's activity within a virtual working environment before the robot will be used in its target actual environment.

articleTitle: Stability and Control Problems in Hydropower Plants
abstract: A standard structure of hydroelectric plant integrates a water reservoir (lake), a tunnel for water delivery and the hydraulic turbine. In many cases water mass oscillation quenching is improved by introducing the surge tank. However this introduction of the surge tank is associated with the addition of a second water conduit - the penstock uniting the surge tank with the hydraulic turbine. In function of the conduit lengths, distributed parameters have to be considered. A structure with two conduits with distributed parameters, surge tank and turbine is quite standard. The present paper deals with such a structure aiming stability and control problems for two types of operation regimes: normal and abnormal. The normal regimes are those with loaded turbine ensuring the frequency/megawatt control of the Electricity Grid while the abnormal consider the water hammer occurring under turbine shutdown. In the normal regimes, controller synthesis is considered to ensure at least stability by the first approximation while in the abnormal regime of water hammer stability and oscillation quenching are ensured by the surge tank only. Both cases are studied using a quadratic Lyapunov functional deduced from the energy identity. A discussion of distributed versus lumped parameters is also done.

articleTitle: Light Fidelity (Li-Fi) Communications Applied to Telepresence Robotics
abstract: Telepresence robots are becoming more and more useful in fields such as education and medicine. Existing applications in telepresence robotics use Wireless Fidelity (WiFi) communications for remote control of the robot and for real-time data exchange. In the Li-Fi system, the data can be transmitted via Visible Light Communication (VLC) system with speeds up to 100 times faster then Wi-Fi. This can be an advantage for robots that have direct visual field for a short period of time (a few seconds) and must transmit mutually consistent data packets. In this paper we are testing the possibility of using the Li-Fi technology on telepresence robots with different mechanical mobility possibilities. An experimental prototype was developed to test the functionality of Li-Fi communications and compare it with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, for the telepresence robots used in education and medicine. Further research will focus on adapting communications protocol so that the large amount of data transmitted by the sender in a short time can be stored and used later by the receiver.

articleTitle: Comparative Numerical Analysis of a Piezoelectric Harvester Based on Non-auxetic and Auxetic Material
abstract: This study presents a comparison of energy harvesting capability of cantilever beam harvester based on non-auxetic and auxetic material. The analysed harvester consisted of two layers: piezoelectric and carrying. Performed numerical calculations allowed to assess influence of an auxetic section in the carrying layer on stress distribution in the piezoelectric and amount of generated electric power. An analysis was conducted for two material variants of the carrying layer: steel and polymer. Presented results showed that energy harvesting efficiency can be increased by introducing auxetic region into the carrying layer of cantilever beam energy harvester.

articleTitle: Implementation of the Precision Beekeeping System for Bee Colony Monitoring in Indonesia and Ethiopia
abstract: Successful implementation of the Precision Beekeeping system includes development of the bee colony monitoring hardware and software for data collection and analysis. This paper focuses on development and installation of such system in two developing countries: Ethiopia and Indonesia. Challenges and peculiarities of the mentioned countries are compared and described in regards of the system installation process, beekeeper's apiary management practices and economic aspects. Bee colony monitoring hardware is based on Raspberry Pi Zero W single board computer as a main controller of the system and connected sensors for temperature, humidity, weight and acoustics. Software part includes cloud-based data warehouse solution with additional models for data analysis and web interface for the remote data monitoring and visualisation. Authors' approach is presented for linking together hardware components with a cloud software into single solution oriented on user needs in target countries. Main purpose of Precision Beekeeping systems is detecting the actual status of the colony and informing the beekeeper in case if unwanted colony behaviour occurs. Another significant aspect of the research is evaluation of the possibility to transfer knowledge and expertise to the experts in target countries. This work is carried out within the SAMS - Smart Apiculture Management Services project, which is funded by the European Union within the H2020-ICT-39-2016-2017 call. To find out more visit the project website https://sams-project.eu/.

articleTitle: Robustness and Muliple Dominant Pole Method
abstract: The paper is devoted to the determination of robust stability regions for PI and PID controllers for first order plants with time delay and integrating plants with time delay. The multiple dominant pole method is considered. The use is shown in the examples.

articleTitle: Techniques for Secure Automated Operation with Cobots Participation
abstract: Each automated operation must be evaluated as safely regarding to the relevant standards and directives to the risk assessment. Particularly, if there is a cobot (collaborative robot) as a main part of workplace. This article concerns the chosen aspects for cobot implementation into the automated workplaces with emphasis to the safety as general and important factor. The article structure describes main techniques for safe operation in order to optimization of workplaces as an industry 4.0 concept. Their implementation is based on a proper understanding of on-site activities in the form of available information about material flow, number of produced components, quality or specific measured values from different sensor types. The information contributes to correct automated innovation implemented as a specified type of cobot with regard to safety as a main factor. The strict separation of robots, humans or other peripheral equipment is currently being phased out with a sensitive integration into group building of automated workplaces. For these reasons, discussions on safety categorization, standards and options for safe operation in automated workplaces are still ongoing.

articleTitle: State-Space Controller as a FOTD Based Generalization of ADRC
abstract: This paper extends ideas of some introductory papers interpreting advanced disturbance rejection control (ADRC) as a generalization of state-space controller design focused on using simplified integral plant models. Advantages achieved by this approach are evaluated by comparing robust constrained controllers based on extended state observer (ESO) design using integrative and first order time delayed (IPDT and FOTD) plant models. Thereby, this comparison may help in discovering new interesting properties of both considered types of resulting controllers. Theoretical analyses is illustrated by real time control of a thermal process.

articleTitle: Position Control with 2DOF PI Controller
abstract: This paper is dealing with an application of two degrees of freedom controller (2DOF) on position control. The focus is to apply optimal weight of the 2DOF PI controllers on real model to improve quality of control process and reduce overshoot. The achieved results on the real model are compared with simulation.

articleTitle: Endpoint Prediction of Basic Oxygen Furnace Steelmaking Based on Gradient of Relative Decarburization Rate
abstract: The contribution deals with the proposal and verification of the endpoint prediction of the basic oxygen furnace steelmaking based on a gradient of relative decarburization rate. The paper briefly describes the steelmaking process in the basic oxygen furnace and the decarburization process. Next, it is proposed to identify the relative decarburization rate and use its gradient to predict the endpoint of the steelmaking process. The algorithm and required inputs are designed and described. Finally, the results of the verification of the prediction of the endpoint of the steelmaking process are presented and analyzed.

articleTitle: Optimal PID Controller Tuning for the Time Delayed Double Integrator
abstract: The paper discusses approaches and results achieved by the performance portrait method in optimal and robust tuning of proportional-integrative-derivative (PID) controllers for the double integrator plus dead time (DIPDT) models. It extends results achieved in tuning proportional-integrative (PI) controller for the integral plus dead time (IPDT) plant models and proportional-derivative (PD) controllers applied to DIPDT plant models. The analysis and optimal tuningby the performance portrait method are using performance measures expressing deviations from piece-wise monotonic ideal output and input shapes. Detail analysis of different design aspects is necessary before starting time-consuming performance portrait generation.

articleTitle: Relay Feedback Identification Method for PID Controller Tuning
abstract: The shifting method of relay feedback identification is a system identification method based on the frequency behaviour of the system. It allows to identify stable or unstable, oscillatory or non-oscillatory systems describable by a second order time delayed model, if these have stable behaviour in the relay feedback test. This paper demonstrates the use of the shifting method to find models of simulated and real systems, including estimation of static gain, also under static disturbances. Identified models could be used for tuning of PID controllers. The models found are compared with prime identified systems according to frequency responses and step responses. The results of the shifting method are compared with the results of other identification methods to verify the practical benefits of use of this method. All tests were done in the programming environments Matlab/Simulink.

articleTitle: The Mathematical Model for Indirect Measurement of Temperature in the Steel-Making Process
abstract: This paper describes the mathematical model for indirect measurement of the melt temperature in the oxygen converter, and his verification. The main task of this model is continuously measurement (prediction) temperature of the melt during the steel-making process in the converter. The change in temperature of the melt is calculated based on the heat balance. The temperature is increased by the heat released from the exothermic reactions of blown oxygen with components of melt. The mathematical model was verified in qualitative terms on the real data.

articleTitle: A Data Mining Approach for Finding Similar Job Positions to Upgrade a Job Position in a System for Evaluating Competencies
abstract: This article focuses on creating an approach to find similar job positions based on an existing job position in a system for evaluating competencies. The proposed method uses data mining methods to find similar job positions on a job portal based on input data. The input data is the job position title and the list of competencies. The proposed approach then accesses the relevant job positions in a job portal and compares them with the entered inputs. The output of the approach is a list of the most similar job positions in the job portal, including their description. Then HR manager should use this output for completing the assigned job position and its competencies. The proposed approach is then experimentally verified.

articleTitle: Smartwatch Based Indoor Localization
abstract: The hardware platform for the indoor pedestrian navigation systems are usually smartphones. They are suitable for the infrastructure-less indoor localization systems since they have several sensors built-in like magnetic compass for direction sensing, gyro and acceleration sensor for motion analysis and Wi-Fi or Bluetooth radio module for fingerprint-based position determination. Some application fields, like monitoring elderly patient's movement, motion path and health condition require more convenient and wearable device like a smartwatch. The smartwatch usually has limited number of sensors and their wearing position make motion sensing less accurate therefore special localization, filtering and data processing algorithms are required. In this article the algorithms, filtering methods and tuning procedures are explained of a smartwatch based indoor localization system.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Biological Signal for Automated Diagnostics
abstract: Thanks to the rapid development of solutions in the field of medical technologies, electrophysiological measurements have become a popular and reliable diagnostic method. Increasing the computing power of processors, their miniaturization and the development of data transmission technologies ushered in a new era of signal processing and sensor production. Both of the above-mentioned phenomena have led to the development of more and more solutions that allow for real-time analysis of large volumes of biological data. The article presents the results of an analysis using statistical tools comparing data recorded by patients with various types of cardiological diseases recorded by the electrocardiological method. The data analyzed are included in the publicly available MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database. The analysis is also the first step in research that will allow to automate the diagnostic process of recognizing heart disease.

articleTitle: High Resolution Large Scale ADC. Case study of an N bit per Volt ADC Implemented using FPAA and FPGA Applied for Precision Altimetery
abstract: Positioning is a hot topic since there is no such system capable of providing accurate position estimation for all environmental cases. This paper treats a new method for the estimation of the altitude for the case of precision vertical displacement. This paper also emphasizes a new analog-to-digital converter (ADC) architecture called N bit per Volt which is a high-resolution large-scale ADC based on a hybridization of analog and digital reconfigurable targets and an analog pressure sensor. It is considered in this document the case of the implementation using the reconfigurable couple FPAA-FPGA capable of processing an input range of 0-4V for a precision of 12 bit and a quantum of 244 uV with a conversion time equal to 31 ADC clock cycles performing a conversion rate of 838.7 kSPs. The solution could find applications on the industrial fields dealing with robotized systems where the ADC could find several applications dealing with large scale analog sensors.

articleTitle: A Real-Time Fail-Safe Algorithm for Decoding of Myoelectric Signals to Control a Prosthetic Arm
abstract: In this article a real-time self-tuning algorithm of detecting fingers movements based on the electromyographic (EMG) sensors is developed. A multi-level input data processing from the EMG sensor with self diagnosis is suggested. It provides the identification of muscle tension, which corresponds of several types of finger movements. This solution enables to use the lowbit controllers to manipulate the prosthetic hand. The results of system modeling and testing on the Arduino nano microcontroller demonstrated that the system identifies finger movements with high accuracy.

articleTitle: Parametric optimization of a Second Order Time Delay System with a PI-Controller
abstract: In the work is posed and solved the parametric optimization problem for second order linear system with delay in control. The control is realised by means of a PI-Controller in the closed loop feedback. It is considered the performance index integral of squared error. The value of the performance index is obtained using of the Lyapunov functional and is equal to the value of the Lyapunov functional at initial function. The Lyapunov functional is determined by means of the Lyapunov matrix. In the paper are presented the optimization results for different time delays and for varies damping factors.

articleTitle: Software Tools to Manage and Simulate Information from the Natural Environment
abstract: In this article, there is presented an application developed in the C# language, for the acquisition, storage of information. The application of data entry and storage developed is based on modern software tools that propose a management solution according to the processing capabilities and needs, but also a real-time analysis of the data. The implemented applications maximize the computing power of the personal PCs in the context of the acquisition of information by usual users. Another perspective consists of the storage of this information in the editable form and the possibility of further analysis. This application is based on the software tools developed in the previous and further stages, depending on the processing needs, it will be possible to optimize the acquisition operation which will mean increasing the number of stored information, but also the possibility of introducing and distributed storage of information.

articleTitle: Filtering Methods for Indoor Magnetic Compass
abstract: The compass is an essential part of any indoor localization system. Many indoor localization systems use smart phone as a hardware platform and they are all equipped with the appropriate magnetic field sensor. As their outdoor counterpart the indoor compass applications are relies on sensing the Earth magnetic field for determining the direction of the magnetic north pole. However, the indoor magnetic field is very inhomogeneous since the metallic structures used in the building construction significantly distorts the magnetic field inside the building. Therefore, the magnetic compass alone is not precise and reliable in indoor environment. To achieve expectable precision several compensations, fine-tuned filtering methods needs to be applied and other information coming from the positioning, motion detection system needs to combined with the magnetic heading information. This article analyses the most significant magnetic compass errors in indoor environment and proposes filtering and error correcting methods together with their tuning methodology.

articleTitle: A Convolutional Method for the Detection of Derivative Discontinuities
abstract: This paper presents a convolutional method for the calculation of a measure for C-n discontinuities at interstitial points. This measure can be used to determine locations where the observational data is discontinuous in the n-th derivative. This is achieved by calculating the Taylor coefficients of the data from the left and right at each interstitial point. The calculation of the Taylor coefficients is constrained to ensure continuity of the model up to degree n-l, while yielding an estimate for the discontinuity of the n-th derivative. These constrains, together with a symmetric support length and a uniform spacing of the observational data, ensure a special block structure of the matrices in the least squares formulation of the minimization problem. This special structure enables an orthogonal residualization corresponding to a generalized Eckart-Young-Mirsky matrix approximation, which then yields a convolutional sequence required to calculate the difference of the n-th Taylor coefficients. Additionally, thanks to the symmetric support length and uniform spacing, it is seen that the convolutional sequences are symmetric or antisymmetric, which ensures a linear phase response. Finally, the results of applying the method to: sensor data emanating from the observation of a drilling process; and synthetic data from a cubic spline with known knots, are presented.

articleTitle: Development of a Controller Unit for Multispectral Imaging System
abstract: This article introduces the development of a controller unit to control a multispectral imaging system applied in an underwater robot for collecting geoscientific data from flooded mines. The paper describes other geoscientific sensors of the robot-platform and explains the theory of the multispectral unit. During the development it was a great challenge to satisfy the size restrictions of the circuit and the delay of the electronics. It is also described that how is this unit works within the robot's system and introduces what we achieved with it during the last 2 years of laboratory and real-environmental testing.

articleTitle: Optimization of Optical Amplification in the High Capacity DWDM System
abstract: In this paper 40 Gbps DWDM (Dense Wavelength Division Multiplex) have been investigated using 16 wavelength channels and an Erbium Doped Fiber Amplifier (EDFA), Raman optical amplifier (ROA) and Semiconductor Optical Amplifier (SOA). Each amplifier type was individually analyzed and the performance has been compared on the basis of transmission performance. The performance of DWDM system is evaluated by the the BER (Bit Error Rate) and Q-factor for individual wavelengths, allocated within the optical C-band (1530 nm - 1565 nm).

articleTitle: Simulation and Fault Detection Techniques for Multilevel Inverters used in Smart Grids
abstract: A smart grid includes a variety of intelligent control systems for power generation and also for increasing the energy efficiency of the system. These systems include smart power converters, but also renewable energy and highly efficient resources. Multilevel inverters are considered modern and basic elements of high voltage power supply systems; however, the failure of electronic power components strongly affects the reliability of the entire system. The important goal in defining and dimensioning of smart grids is the measuring and determining of the boundary conditions and operating regimes of the power components. This paper presents an innovative technique for the fault detection of power components for a three-phase multilevel inverter, which is one of the typical components of a smart grid. Single, double and triple switch failures can be diagnosed by this method. The detection mechanism is based on the analysis of the stator current, with the possibility to differentiate between the simple and multiple switching failures. The paper also approaches multilevel converter models, which are systematically made from basic components and use configurable subsystems to switch between architectures of different converter topologies. Also, these models can achieve the harmonic analysis to verify the system correctness and can simulate different operational scenarios to test the functioning of the control system.

articleTitle: LiFi Technology Feasibility Study for Car-2-Car Communication
abstract: The car-2-car communication is one functionality already accepted by most important car manufacturers as a “must have” for the next generation of cars. Such a functionality will increase the road safety by enhancing drivers awareness about road conditions and eventual obstacles. It can be also used to inform the cars behind about risky situations in order to trigger early avoidance actions (e.g. breaking). In order to standardize this type of communication, it was created the Car2Car Communication Consortium who's task is to choose between multiple technologies and design a common architecture which allows cars communication between different OEMs. The current paper presents an analysis of the LiFI technology applied to car-2-car communication: it is proposed a new solution for the implementation which is an extension of a functionality already available in new cars: automatic high beam controller.

articleTitle: Efficient Radio Map Update Algorithm for Indoor Localization
abstract: The GPS, location-based services and navigation systems are well known terms in the case of outdoor environment. In the recent years the location-based services in indoor environment are gaining more attention as well. Since there is no GPS like, widely available technology for indoor localization, several methods were developed in the past. One of the very popular method is using some existing radio infrastructure like Wi-Fi inside a building and creating the signal strength map of those radio transmitters. Since the field strength is location dependent for each radio station, measuring the RSSI value the location of the receiver can be estimated. However, collecting and maintaining time-to-time a relatively large field strength database is a challenging task. To ease this work and increase the overall performance of such a localization system we investigate the motion classification and floorplan constrains algorithm effectiveness to update the field strength map. The overall performance of the localization system is evaluated in the terms of the maintenance of the fingerprint database using real life localization scenarios.

articleTitle: Control of Battery Operated Drive
abstract: This paper describes possibility of efficiency enhancement of electrical drives in general, especially in mobile robotics application. The vector control is traditional algorithm, but thanks to the Maximum Torque per Ampere criterion, must be the control algorithm modified properly. The paper describes feasibility of this algorithm and verification on mathematical model. These methods can be used for permanent magnet synchronous machines in over speed area.

articleTitle: The Experimental Model of the Cantilever Beam with Piezoelectric Patch Elements
abstract: This paper discusses the approach of transporting from a real test stand of cantilever beam containing a piezoelectric actuator and sensor into the Simulink model and at the same time use this model to design an observer to observe separated modes. The fixed end of the beam is excited using the kinematic exciter while Doppler Laser is used for calibration. Experimental identification is made by using the Discrete Fourier Transform and the Simulink model is made using the State Space modeling. The aim was to create a simple and easy to understand tool for testing, debugging and a better understanding of new control algorithms.

articleTitle: Proposed Model for a Microservices Cluster
abstract: The main goal of this proposed paper was to approach the dependable systems domain, to be more specific to improve their availability attributes. The proposed solution is based on four Raspberry Pi boards (one master and three slaves). This infrastructure was chosen in order to comply with the highest level of scalability that can be triggered automatically by the thresholds set and can be done both horizontally and vertically. We have to mention that our proposed solution it can be also used as a monitoring and an alerting tool when custom thresholds are violated by the system/applications.

articleTitle: Utilization Of Deep Learning For Wear Analysis Of Mechanical Components Using Self-Oscillating Vibroacoustic Systems
abstract: A common method of conducting non-destructive testing of the technical condition of mechanical components is to use the measurement of acoustic waves generated during the operation of machines and devices. The analysis of the frequency spectrum of the signal allows you to estimate the degree of wear of elements such as shafts, bearings or tools used in machine tools. In traditional applications, it is required to make a measurement during the work of the tested element, which is often associated with a time-consuming process of placing measuring devices with the risk of damage to the sensors used, or the health and life of the person carrying out the measurement. For this reason, modern methods of vibroacoustic wear analysis are based on acoustic wave generation systems that allow to obtain accurate measurements without having to take measurements in machinery and equipment operating conditions.The solution to this problem is the use of self-excited systems, which are characterized by lower requirements of measuring equipment and very high sensitivity. The amplitude and frequency of vibrations excited in the system can be constant for a long period of time, which significantly facilitates the collection of measurements. Based on the analysis of the amplitude and frequency of modulated signals generated by the system, it is possible to determine changes in the structure of materials caused by stress or fatigue wear.

articleTitle: Fractional Linear Prediction Toolbox for MATLAB
abstract: This paper presents the Fractional Linear Prediction (FLP) Toolbox implemented in MATLAB with a supporting livescript interface that offers an user-friendly environment for the prediction of one-dimensional signals. Two versions of the FLP are implemented in the toolbox and presented here. While the first approach is using the “full” memory (the whole history of the signal), the second approach uses the “restricted” memory (two, three or four previous samples). Both FLP approaches are compared to the standard linear prediction and their performance is evaluated in examples using a test signal (sine wave signal), and a real-data signal (speech signal) as the input.

articleTitle: Overview of Reinforcement Learning and its Application in Control Theory
abstract: This article is an overview of the emerging reinforcement learning technology. This technology has been quickly developing in the last years, and it has a great industrial potential since it can manage tasks that were unable to control by conventional technology. The article also includes an overview of neural network processors available on the market, which are much more efficient to solve artificial intelligence tasks than standard CPU.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Biological (EMG) Signal
abstract: Electromyography (EMG) is an electrophysiological field of knowledge that operates through bioelectrical signals from muscles. The signals are registered with the use of surface or needle electrodes and can be later analysed to detect myopathic or neuropathic lesions. The diagnosis might be performed through numerical parameters. This thesis contains the analysis of EMG signals divided into three groups: registered with the use of needle electrodes, generated through computer simulation and registered by surface electrodes. In the first two groups there can be distinguished six signals: two from healthy muscles, two from muscles with myopathic lesions and two from muscles with neuropathic lesions. All signals registered with surface electrodes come from healthy muscles. Signals gathered by needle electrodes are decomposed through a computer algorithm which brings out motor unit action potentials (MUAPs). Numerical parameters connected with amplitude and time are calculated from MUAPs and compared with nominal values. The analytical method for signals registered by surface electrodes is called the Clustering Index method. The analysis presents that 100 % of signals registered by needle electrodes come from muscles with lesions which is not completely accurate whereas 100 % of the signals remaining are from healthy muscles.

articleTitle: Reaching Law Based DSMC Strategies: Robustness Comparison
abstract: Sliding mode control strategies are an efficient method of ensuring robustness of the system with respect to disturbance and model uncertainties. The robustness property of such strategies is achieved by driving the representative point of the controlled plant into a narrow vicinity of a properly selected sliding hyperplane. Consequently, the width of this vicinity is the most commonly used performance index in sliding mode control. This index is closely related to the so-called sliding variable, which is a constructed output of the plant. On the other hand, in practical applications we may often require exact information about system state error, which is not explicitly considered in sliding mode control. Motivated by this problem, in this paper we explore the relation between quasi-sliding mode band width and maximum error of all state variables. In that way, we provide a more tangible performance comparison tool based on the previously published results on sliding mode control. In particular, we analyze state errors for a number of established strategies and demonstrate that these errors are proportional to the quasi-sliding mode band width.

articleTitle: The use of Kalman Filter in Control the Balancing Robot
abstract: In this paper describes a project of the gimbal which allows stabilizing devices such a video recorder, sport camera or smartphone during recording video clips. Function of this kind of stabilization including photography and robotics was presented in the introduction. As well as, this chapter includes purpose and scope of the each step of a design process. The next chapter is devoted to discussion of existing commercial solutions and specifying their advantages and disadvantages. Constructional features, that were used in the design of the mechanical part, were specified in the predesign phase based on the carried out review. The third chapter is devoted to the full process of designing devices. The first step was to create a mechanical structure in the CAD program, diagnostics of possible constructional errors and then realising a real mechanical system. Next, the author discusses elements of the electrical system and mutual connection and communication. The next part of the thesis is devoted to description of the way of data reading in the used sensors and the way of their filtration. The rest of the chapter is devoted to the control of the mechanical system. Starting from a linearity testing, through a mathematical model identification and at the end carrying out of control of the system both by a simulation and on physical device. The next chapter is devoted to testing control influence on device stabilization quality and correlating the data.

articleTitle: Development of a Robust Wireless Mesh Network Modules for Proximity Sensing During Assembly Process of a Steam Turbine
abstract: This paper deals with a design of wireless proximity sensing between the stator and rotor of a steam turbine during a final steps of an assembly. The result of this assembly process is an optimal setting of the seal which affects overall turbine efficiency. An innovative approach including internet of things (IoT) principles and mesh network topology has been used to transmit critical data to the supervisor. A few working prototypes have been created and tested in real production in cooperation with an industrial partner.

articleTitle: Reduced-Order State Observers for Linear Discrete-time Positive Systems
abstract: For linear discrete-time positive systems the paper proposes an approach reflecting structural system constraints and positiveness in solving the problem of reduced-order positive observer design. Common system parameter constraints are represented in the form of linear matrix inequalities, combined with observer $\mathrm{H}_{\infty}$ norm bound, to guarantee the observer asymptotic stability. A numerical example is included to assess the feasibility of the proposed technique.

articleTitle: Discrete-time Linear Systems Fault Diagnosis Using Schmidt-Kalman Filters
abstract: The paper introduces a modified form of Schmidt-Kalman filter, suitable for discrete-time linear systems. Partiallyupdated state of the Schmidt-Kalman filter is introduced to consider additive parameter changes in fault detection filter to be unbiased. The presented modification of the Schmidt-Kalman filter relations, and its reformulation, construct so useful tool in fault-detection application for plants with small subsystem interactions. The proposed method that accomplishes this is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Approaches for Dynamic Representation of Mathematical Content in Engineering Education
abstract: In this paper we present two approaches for enhancing digital study materials for engineering education and show how they can be transformed from basic, static documents into interactive, dynamic documents. Nowadays, non-traditional teaching methods such as flipped learning, blended learning, project-based learning are being introduced into engineering lectures and this trend found its way into mathematics courses. These methods place emphasis more on self-study and out-of classroom preparation before the actual exercise in a classroom setting occurs. They involve usage of additional media that complement classic course textbooks or study materials in printed or digital form. We show that the static digital documents itself can be enhanced by dynamic elements. First, we discuss ways of using well-known LATEX typesetting system for creating dynamic, animated algebraic representations and 2D graphs for visualizing mathematical expressions, exporting and publishing them as a PDF document, which can be made available online. Second, we show how JavaScript-based reactive elements interactively link algebraic with graphical representations in HTML documents, making the study material an active reading experience.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of Preload Effect in a Piezoelectric Cantilever Energy Harvester on Energy Harvesting Performance
abstract: One of the factors limiting performance of PZT material in energy harvesting applications is its tensile strength, which limits its maximum allowable strain. In typical cantilever beam harvester the piezoelectric patch placed on the beam is periodically stretched and compressed during vibrations. Exceeding specific value of tensile stress leads to damage of piezoelectric material and impairment of its energy conversion capabilities. One of the distinct properties of all ceramics, also PZT, is exhibiting low strength in tension but, simultaneously, very high compressive strength. Aim of this work was to introduce initial compressive stress into piezoelectric layer, therefore increasing allowable beam deflection during vibration. To determine effect of piezoelectric patch prestressing on harvester performance a series of numerical simulations were done.

articleTitle: Active Protection Against Overturning in Uneven Terrain for the Mars Rover Analogue
abstract: The purpose of the article is to describe the research on the system of quick and autonomous response to the danger of overturning the robot or exceeding the safe swing angle. Chapter II describes its construction, identifies situations that can cause a deflection above the permissible level and reactions to occurring events. The chapter ends with a drawing showing an algorithm in which special emphasis has been placed on safety, so as not to lead to the opposite effect than planned, even if the robot does not detect a situation identical to that anticipated when designing the system. Chapter III describes the tests, presents graphs with driving parameters for all cases. Chapter IV summarizes the research and presents ideas for further development of the system.

articleTitle: Road Condition Monitoring with Use of MEMS Based Unit
abstract: The paper deals with the design and use of smart unit for real-time road condition monitoring. The basis is three-axis accelerometer, gyroscope and magnetometer based on MEMS technology, which provides its data to the main microcontroller. As a communication interface for data providing, the high-speed CAN bus was used. The reason was an easier way to implement in the car and achieve a higher frequency of data provision. The result of this work is the determination of the critical sections of the measured route.

articleTitle: Identification of Power Profiles for Small Home Photovoltaic Power Plant Based on Similarity Network
abstract: Small home photovoltaic power plants are now becoming increasingly popular. Their expansion is caused by a very competitive price and effort to preferring using ecological energy sources in society. For the best use of produced energy, it is necessary to know how the photovoltaic power plant behaves throughout the year. Possibility to find patterns in energy production could help us make a model of behaviour this power source and efficiently plan the consumption of energy without overflow of energy to the grid. In this paper, we used an approach based on similarity networks to identify power profiles for a small photovoltaic power plant.

articleTitle: Task Scheduling Algorithm for Renovation Teams of Water Distribution Systems
abstract: A lack of continuity in the water supply system can have many negative effects on the consumers and the entire water supply company. This paper describes problems associated with interruptions in this process and makes use of the Water Network Tool for Resilience (WNTR) library. This library allows modelling and simulating water distribution process after a disaster event. Using hydraulic model implemented in EPANET, input data such as the list of failures, number of repair teams, equipment available etc. the algorithm helps to determine the order of repairs to be made so as to restore the continuity of the water supply process in the shortest possible time.

Author Keywords: Task Scheduling Algorithm Water Distribution System Water Distribution Process

articleTitle: Reference Sliding Variable Based Discrete-Time Sliding Mode Control
abstract: The study considers the problem of sliding mode controller design for sampled-data systems with disturbances. We propose a new discrete-time switching type control scheme using a predesigned evolution of the sliding variable as a reference and a trajectory following reaching law. We show that this approach ensures the existence of the quasi-sliding mode in the sense of Gao et al. Additionally, under the assumption of boundedness and smoothness of continuous-time disturbance, we complete our strategy with a disturbance compensator. It's aim is to calculate the previous disturbance value based on the current and previous state measurement, and use it to compensate for the disturbance in the current step. Finally, we prove that the application of this compensator leads to the reduction of the quasi-sliding mode band width to O(T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) order. The effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is verified with a simulation example.

articleTitle: Proprioceptive Force Sensing Adapted on High-Ratio Custom Actuators in Quadrupedal Walking Robot
abstract: Proprioceptive force sensing is a common practice among quadruped robot designers as it requires no additional components mounted on the legs. Yet it is usually adapted with actuators that have relatively low mechanical gear ratio, lower than 10:1. Tests performed in this paper show the proprioceptive technique adapted on a custom 22:1 brushless actuator with cycloidal gear. The aim is to successfully use this technique for setting and measuring forces acting on the end effector of the leg in order to detect contacts and perform a rough force control.

articleTitle: Anisotropy-based Estimation Problem for Linear Discrete Time Varying Systems with Multiplicative Noises: Special Case
abstract: In this paper, the anisotropy-based estimation problem for linear discrete time varying multiplicative noises systems is considered for the two special cases of estimator model. The anisotropy-based bounded real lemma for both special cases is obtained in state-space. The estimation problem is reduced to linear matrix inequalities solution problem.

articleTitle: Moving Ground as a Disturbance to Human Balance
abstract: Obtaining a vertical position of the body is a property that man obtained in the process of evolution. Thanks to this, locomotion on two legs has become possible, and thus more or less complicated manipulation operations. Thus, it can be concluded that the ability to maintain balance is one of the most basic skills, and any imbalance significantly limits human mobility and independence. Keeping the body upright is not always easy and the constant force of gravity can lead to a fall. Thanks to the phenomenon of proprioception, i.e. deep feeling, controlling human reflexes without his awareness, it is possible to maintain a safe margin of stability, which in turn will allow the realization of the activity of the motor organ. The human movement organ is very complicated, and the description of its operation includes issues in the field of mechanics, anatomy and physiology. For this reason, models with varying degrees of complexity are used to analyze motion, allowing the simplification of the actual structure of the human body while maintaining postural interactions. These types of models are often used in the design of robotic motion support systems that could improve assistance to people with physical disabilities in the future. The article presents the approach to modeling human balance in the case when the substrate on which the patient stands is moving harmonically.

articleTitle: Monitoring and Controlling Home Appliances by Different Network Technologies
abstract: The paper presents a smart home system using relatively easily accessible resources and characterized by reasonable prices, such as Raspberry Pi3, WeMos-D1 board and Interactive Graphical SCADA System (IGSS). The developed solution is also characterized by several advantages related to its maintenance over time, as well as the existence of facilities in use for the people living in such a smart home, whether they are old persons or have certain disabilities. The purpose of the present research was to achieve a centralized control system of the various devices in the smart home under the control of the IGSS. In particular, the aim was to minimize physical wiring and the predominant use of wireless networks, the permanent remote control of all domestic devices and appliances, as well as monitoring of their current operating status.

articleTitle: A DFT Computation Method for the Real-Time Processing of Vibration Signals at FPGA Circuit Level
abstract: The paper proposes a DFT (Discret Fourier Transform) calculation method implemented in an FPGA (Field Programmable Gate Array) circuit. The possibilities of parallel processing in the FPGA circuits generate new approaches for data processing. Normally, FFT processing needs all series of samples of a signal to evaluate the result. Due to the complexity and the large volume of computation, the time required for processing is significant. Thus, the acquisition time of a sequence of samples is summed with the processing time, which practically leads to an off-line processing, in relation to the moment of occurrence of an event in a process. The proposed method tries to obtain the result of the FFT processing in parallel with vibration signal acquisition. Thus, the processing is performed in real-time, at the acquisition speed of the vibration signal.

articleTitle: Automatic Navigation System for 3D Robotic Laser Cladding
abstract: This paper presents an innovative approach to 3D robotic laser cladding of complex workpieces. To begin, the article brings a brief introduction to the problem and discusses the current state-of-the-art. Next, there is a description of the proposed algorithm which uses data from a 2D laser profile scanner mounted on a laser cladding head carried by a robotic manipulator to create a 3D model of the workpiece. Afterwards, the model is used to generate trajectories for the laser cladding head in order to create a continuous layer of weld beads to protect the surface of the original workpiece. The algorithm was developed to apply a layer of stellite to the leading edge of a steam turbine blade in order to increase its wear resistance. The results of the real application are presented in the last part of the paper.

articleTitle: Application of PLC Controller for a Deflection Control of a Piezoelectric Cantilever Actuator
abstract: Article presents the experimental investigation on application of programmable logic controller (PLC) for a deflection control of a piezoelectric cantilever actuator. The piezoelectric actuator contained a composite cantilever beam and a voltage amplifier. The cantilever beam was built by gluing of Macro Fiber Composite patch and a rectangular carrying material. A deflection of beam tip of this cantilever beam was an controlled variable in tested piezoelectric actuator. On the basis of laboratory experiments results, it can be concluded, PLC controller enabled an effective control of deflection of the piezoelectric cantilever actuator, which was used in laboratory experiments. Standard PLC controller can be used in industry for a deflection control of piezoelectric cantilever actuator instead of some real-time device. PLC controller can be also used in scientific laboratory experiments.

articleTitle: Influence of Soil Parameters on Protein Presence for a Mars Rover Analogue’s On-Board Laboratory Setup
abstract: The purpose of our work is to examine the impact of parameters such as humidity, temperature or pH value of soil on the presence of organic substances in it - proteins. The reason for our research is the improvement of protein detection methods in the rover analogue laboratory. We decided to use temperature, humidity and pH sensors for the measurements. The tests were carried out on a permanent soil composition with variable, artificially induced combinations parameters. To identify the proteins, chose to use biuret reaction and microscopic observations. We predicted that high soil temperature would destroy protein, higher humidity should accelerate reactions, depending on the pH of the solution, they will behave as acids (in alkaline solution) or as bases (in acidic solution). Results of tests proved our initial assumption right.

articleTitle: Processing and Analysis of Accelerometer Data for the Surface State Identification
abstract: Surface state monitoring is a difficult and complex issue. Installation of the large number of static sensors is probable solution but huge size of the road network makes application of static methods challenging in terms of cost and labor. Authors of this article propose to use “mobile solutions“ for the purpose of surface state identification. They provide an overview of the existing methods of data processing in combination with hardware, which could be used for the objective of surface defects identification. All of the algorithms were tried on real test datasets collected by measuring unit. Further research suggests the application of the most suitable approaches in autonomous mobile platforms projects.

articleTitle: Experimental SCADA Platform Using Digital Signatures
abstract: This paper presents the development of an experimental platform for simulating the use of digital signatures between the typical SCADA components: master and remote terminal units, based on the DNP3 communication protocol.

articleTitle: Online Emissivity Estimation of the Hollow Cathode and the Treated Part in the HC Plasma Nitriding Process
abstract: Modeling the thermal process in the Hollow Cathode Anodic Plasma Nitriding (HCAPN) is essential for control. The heat transfer mechanism consists mainly of conduction by gas and radiation. The essential parameter of the heat radiation is the emissivity of the metal surface. It was shown that the emissivity of the commonly used metals (carbon steel, aluminum) is highly temperature dependent and in the case of surface heat-treatment, the modification of the surface structure modify the emissivity also. The goal of the paper is to present an online emissivity estimation method using Extended Kalman Filter, thus a simultaneous state and parameter estimator. For this, an augmented state-space model will be used. The HCAPN setup consist of a hollow cathode and the treated part, in most cases having different materials, thus the algorithm was developed to estimate the emissivity of both materials.

articleTitle: Identification of the Heating Process in Differential Scanning Calorimeter with the Use of Hammerstein Model
abstract: Differential thermal analysis method and appropriate heating model are presented. Next, the general description of designed and constructed device (by Authors) - Differential Scanning Calorimeter (DSC) is given. It is used to determine some thermal properties of physical modern materials (i.e. glass/softening temperature in chalcogenide glasses). Modeling of heating process with non-linear properties, observed in device, required in thermal analysis is considered in this paper, where a block Hammerstein structure is selected to describe both dynamic and non-linear properties of phenomenon. A parametric identification method with least squares and SVD decomposition approaches is proposed. The chosen method has been experimentally tested and numerically compared with the linear (FIR) model for real data.

articleTitle: Porous Functions Toolbox for MATLAB
abstract: A new mathematical tool, porous functions, has been suggested recently (Podlubny, I., ”Porous Functions”, Fractional Calculus & Applied Analysis, vol. 22, no. 6, pp. 1502-1516, 2019). In this paper we introduce the Porous Functions Toolbox for MATLAB, which serves for evaluation of porous functions, their visualization, and basic operations with such functions in one-and two-dimensional case. The fields of potential application of these new tools include granular materials; colloids, liquid crystals, emulsions, foams; polymers, textiles, rubber, glass; rock layers, sediments, oil, soil; biopolymers and biological materials, etc. Most recently, fractional-order elements and controllers are manufactured using various kinds of layered and fractal-like structures, graphenes, nanocomposites, and MXenes, which can be modeled using the porous functions approach.

articleTitle: Controlling a Bank Model Economy by Using an Adaptive Model Predictive Control with Help of an Extended Kalman Filter
abstract: This paper describes a bank-customer model and proposes a control scheme algorithm which guarantees to obtain a desired capital to asset ratio. The used control system is an Adaptive Model Predictive Control (MPC). The MPC offers the possibility to control the error between capital/asset ratio and the ratio required by the bank under the Basel regulatory framework, which should converge to zero. The uncertainties of the model are estimated by an Extended Kalman Filter and the model is online adapted to realize the prediction.

articleTitle: Control of a Rotary Flexible Joint Experiment based on Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper presents the Reinforcement Learning (RL) technique for control of a Flexible Joint Experiment. In the firs part of the paper an overview of the field of Reinforcement Learning in the frame of Machine Learning context and some basic RL strategies for control are highlighted. The design of RL controllers for linear systems is briefly presented. The RL based on two neural networks is designed for an experiment that consists of a DC motor and a rigid beam with flexible joint. The goal of the control system is that the beam tap to follow a predefined trajectory. The experimental setup is a nonlinear system, but in order to tune the controller parameters, a linear model is derived. The controller performances are evaluated using a real plant experiment. In the last sections of the paper the results obtained by numerical simulation and the main conclusions regarding the performance of the control system are presented.

articleTitle: The Efficiency of Adaptive Filters to Noise-Suppression Inside a Small Cavity
abstract: Usually, the simulation demonstrates the efficiency of adaptive filters used for noise canceling. The output of the adaptive filter cancels the undesired fault signal to zero by calculation. The paper shows the real efficiency of adaptive filtration in the state where noise and anti-noise are transmitted to a small cavity and at the same time, the residual noise measures by a microphone inside the cavity. This measurement allows for evaluating the remaining sound pressure level. The paper will compare experimentally and analytically the efficiency of the used adaptive filter.

articleTitle: Optimization of Controller Parameters by Simulation Model for Rotary-Hearth Furnace
abstract: Rotary hearth furnace serves for heating steel charge stored on rotary hearth and belongs to group industry furnaces with a big energy consumption. The intermittent rotary movement of the hearth is the main source of disturbances, which makes it difficult to control the furnace. Common dynamic characteristics that are difficult for PI, PID controllers include large time delays and high-order dynamics. The complex dynamic model appears as suitable tool for design control system of this furnace. There is exploited simulation model of this furnace for design controllers and optimisation controller parameters. The advantage of this approach with a complex simulation model is easier design of optimally operating controllers. At the same time the disadvantage is the great time consuming solution of optimally working controllers on the computer.

articleTitle: Innovative Acoustical Diagnostic System Compatible With Industry 4.0 Standards
abstract: Industry 4.0 which a characteristic feature is disappearance of the barrier between humans and machines, the use of cloud computing and the dissemination of so-called “Internet of Things” (IoT) enables global access to data and machines. An important pillar of Industry 4.0 is “machine intelligence”, which implies the autonomy of production processes, which can also include the organization of production and response to changes or prediction of the damages in demand for a product with specific parameters. This paper presents an intelligent diagnostic system, which is dedicated for implementation in Industry 4.0 ecosystem. The main feature of this solution is the Cloud communication enables Cloud computing of the predictive maintenance algorithms for the health monitoring of the construction under examination.

articleTitle: Unified Software Interface for Numerical Evaluation of Integrals and Derivatives of Fractional Order
abstract: This work presents an unified software interface for numerical evaluation of integrals and derivatives of fractional order implemented as live-script in the MATLAB environment. The proposed FracApp tool merges several different approaches freely downloadable from the MathWorks MATLAB Central File Exchange portal, by including their input parameters in the function call, and furthermore it allows enhancements by including new numerical methods. All used approaches are compared to analytic solution by solving a standard test problem, and the approximation precision of the numerical methods is displayed graphically and evaluated numerically.

articleTitle: The Inherent Velocity Limitation in Robust Robot Control
abstract: The aim of this paper is to show an original method of the velocity limitation in robust MIMO motion system based on the theory of variable structure control. The advantage of the presented approach is in its usability for both the fixed target control and the command following one. Furthermore, we provide a continuous modification of the control algorithm suitable for engineering practice, where the motion velocity limitation for the safety and integrity of the technology is required. Numeric simulation on the robot dynamic model illustrates the quality and the reliability of the presented control method.

articleTitle: D-stability of Linear Stochastic Systems with State-Space Forms
abstract: In this paper LMI based design conditions, factored by D-stability circular region, are derived for stability analysis and state feedback control of stochastic systems with state-space form reflecting state multiplicative noise. Specific expression of the controller matrix gain for stochastic stabilization is analyzed in the sense of mean square stability, while the effect of the given structure is more pronounced. A nontrivial example is provided to illustrate the control scheme development and noise suppression task.

articleTitle: Hybrid Control for Semi-Active Suspension Design of a Railway Vehicle
abstract: This paper investigates the suspension performance for a high-speed railway vehicle based on a half-car vehicle model. The dynamic responses are studied for the track conditions provided by Federal Rail Administration (FRA) report, and are compared with rail deflection measurements collected from the Konya-Polatli high-speed rail line in Turkey. A hybrid control scheme based on skyhook and groundhook methodologies is proposed to ably substitute the expensive active suspension designs. Then, a multi-objective optimization problem is formulated and the bi-state damping coefficients are synthesized by using the Gradient and LMI optimization based algorithms. Numerical studies show that the semi-actively controlled suspension system can achieve a performance highly comparable to an actively-controlled vehicle even for severe track excitations. Besides it can offer considerable benefits on the ride quality by maintaining a soft vertical ride and realible driving conditions.

articleTitle: Smith Predictor Based Fractional Integral-Fractional Derivative Controller Tuning for Interval First Order Transfer Functions with Time Delay
abstract: This manuscript provides a frequency-domain control methodology to tune the parameters of a fractional integral-fractional derivative (FIFD) controller, which is developed based on a Smith predictor (SP) control structure. For compensating the interval first order time-delayed processes, this paper proposes a novel technique and provides a practical approach. By profiting from the proposed systematic way, not only the controller parameters can optimally be determined to satisfy the desired control system performance specifications under the perturbed conditions, but also the stability margins of the system, i.e., the phase margin and the gain crossover frequency, are tunable. A necessary and sufficient condition is also achieved for the robust stability of the closed-loop control system. Using simulation, the results obtained by applying the proposed technique are given to show the application and the effectiveness of the paper's novelties.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Integral System Control
abstract: This paper deals with the control of a nonlinear integral system in the form of a DC electric motor with worm gear and a microcontroller-based control unit. The aim is to control the angle of rotation of the output shaft. The paper tries to describe the nonlinearity of the system, which is caused by the typical characteristics of DC electric motors. The solution includes identification of the system and its nonlinearities and application of a PID controller algorithm. The influence of nonlinearities is verified by comparison of a simulation in MATLAB / Simulink environment and an experiment on a physical model.

articleTitle: Recommendation Systems with Machine Learning
abstract: Recommender systems are a subclass of information filtering systems. These systems are specialized software components, which usually make part of a larger software system, but can also be standalone tools. A recommender system's main goal is to provide the user software suggestions for items that can be useful. The suggestions are related to different decision-making mechanisms, different techniques, such as, what product to buy, what movie to watch, or what vacation to reserve. In the context of recommender systems, the general term “item” refers to what the system is actually recommending to its users. The paper presents the development and the comparison of multiple recommendation systems, capable of making item suggestions, based on user, item and user-item interaction data, using different machine learning algorithms. Also, the paper deals with finding different ways of using machine learning models to create recommendation systems, training, evaluating and comparing the different methods in order to provide a general but accurate solution for ranking prediction.

articleTitle: Software Architecture for a Mobile Robot designed for Rescue Missions Support in Hazardous Environments
abstract: The rescue missions after incidents in hazardous industrial environments (chemical, explosive, ore mines) imposes a high risk for rescuers, while the incidents specifics are different from case to case. Once that the incident occurs, it is essential to determine what happened, what is the current situation and how the incident may develop in the immediate and near future. This understanding of the incident allows the rescue teams to plan and intervene for the rescue of affected persons. Nowadays, there are more and more demands for mobile platforms, teleoperated or even with autonomous functions, which to assist rescue teams in responses to those incidents, by gathering real time information about the incident causes and development, or by logistically assisting the rescue teams. This paper presents the software architecture for a mobile platform for detection of shock waves generated by explosions.

articleTitle: Threat Objects Detection in Airport using Machine Learning
abstract: Airports operate under high demands and strive to satisfy many diverse, interrelated performance goals. Airport areas, such as security and safety also refer to detecting hazardous materials inside passengers' luggage. This topic is independent to the size of the airport and presents a high importance. The detection of threat objects using X-ray luggage scan images is a big part of aviation security. Currently most screenings are still based on the manual detection of potential threat objects, and rely heavily on the human experts. Artificial intelligence is often used to describe machines that mimic cognitive human functions such as learning and problem solving. At this moment, the most interesting branch of artificial intelligence is automatic learning, allowing computers to learn to solve problems on their own. Machine learning (ML) made a series of discoveries that once seemed impossible, such as: recognizing the human voice, search engines, filtering out unsolicited messages, recognizing human face, medical diagnostics, creating realistic photos of people (using a set of photos, the algorithm creates new faces, practically inventing them), analyzing the stock market, recognizing objects, etc. The paper presents the implementation of a threat objects recognition system using the convolutional neural network and specialized libraries in ML such as OpenCV and Keras with TensorFlow. The topics presented are the development of the convolutional neural network, used data augmentation techniques, tests and detection rate using X-ray images.

articleTitle: Application of Web-based Immersive Virtual Reality in Mathematics Education
abstract: This paper deals with design and implementation of web-based, virtual reality (WebVR) application MathworldVR for teaching higher mathematics concepts that require spatial abilities. It describes the use of methods and approaches of instrumental interaction within VR through direct visual manipulation of input variables of parametrized functions, which shortens the time needed for students to understand the underlying principles of a given mathematical theory. Advantages, disadvantages and limitations of developing VR applications for the web in contrast to native desktop applications are discussed. We outline the utilization of A-Frame framework together with the JavaScript library React for fast VR prototyping. Individual components defining the MathworldVR 3D user interface within virtual environment (VE) are presented and we show how various two handed interaction techniques help in the process of teaching mathematics.

articleTitle: Multivariable Adaptive Control Strategy for an Activated Sludge Process Inside a Wastewater Treatment Plant
abstract: This study addresses an innovative multivariable control strategy for a wastewater treatment bioprocess with activated sludge. This bioprocess takes place in a continuous reactor located at the Wastewater Treatment Plant Făcăi, Romania. The proposed adaptive control structure is designed under realistic assumptions: several process variables are unavailable, the reaction kinetics is time-varying and unknown, the influent pollutant flow rate varies in large limits and much more its concentration is totally unknown. The novelty of the approach consists in the insertion of a sliding mode observer (SMO) in overall control structure. The SMO provides the estimates of the unknown influent pollutant concentration. The performance of the adaptive multivariable control algorithm is assessed via numerical simulations based on data provided from the plant.

articleTitle: Finding Optimal Sensor Positions for Hand-Eye Calibration
abstract: A hand-eye calibration is used to find the relative position between a robot flange and a mounted sensor, which is a very important knowledge for the automatic control of robotic laser welding systems. Most of the articles deal with a mathematical solution of the equation AX = XB, but also the input relative changes of flange positions A and sensor positions B are an important factor for calibration accuracy. Mainly the errors of the matrices A and B, which depend on the specific calibration positions. This paper first describes the parameters affecting the accuracy of matrices A and B. Subsequently, the proposal of the optimal generator of the calibration positions is presented. The proposed algorithm is finally verified in simulations.

articleTitle: Predicting Safety Logic Device Solutions via Decision Trees and Rules Algorithms
abstract: Considering the extensive data sets and statistical techniques, a digital factory (plant) embodies a branch of machine learning that has an impact on machine safety. We propose a study based on an application of decision trees and rules algorithms (JRIP, J48, Random Forest, Random Tree, and PART). Our experimental data were collected from various industrial machine safety solutions. Diverse validation techniques were employed to derive the classification performance of each method; the approach is expected to simplify the user choice of a suitable safety logic device type. In this study, the overall classification methods proportion of individual safety logic device solutions were correctly assigned by using the training-evaluated test mode, and the prediction accuracy reached 100%; further, when assessing the 5-fold cross-validation test mode, we obtained the success rate of 82% (JRIP and PART). PART as the best method was correctly assigned for the 10-fold cross-validation test mode (85%). New developments within the broad province of machine learning, including the concepts characterized in our study, may facilitate effective assessment of machine safety systems.

articleTitle: Statistical Process Control in Big Data Environment
abstract: Big data analysis tools are an inevitable part of instruments and methods for monitoring and predicting the longitudinal performance of the processes in the production systems of the future, based on the deep automatization and overall digitalization. From this point of view statistical process control (SPC) will continue to be very effective method for meeting these goals. But there must be done some modifications. This paper deals with such possible modifications of SPC. In the first part of the paper the stress is put on various methods that can be integrated into SPC to meet new challenges in collecting, analysing and interpreting data (control charts for high yield processes, multivariable approaches, profile monitoring, data mining tools including machine learning methods, nonparametric control charts). SW for the selected discussed methods is also mentioned. The second part of the paper is devoted to the nonparametric methods of SPC and to the methodology of their practical application.

articleTitle: TrueTime-based Analysis of the Communication Networks used in Vehicle Control Structures
abstract: Control through communication networks, e.g., local interconnect network (LIN), controller area network (CAN), FlexRay, Ethernet, in automotive systems has become a necessity nowadays. Although the advantages brought by their introduction worth the implementation, there are also some disadvantages. Their adverse effects on the performances and stability of control systems have to undergo serious analysis and design w.r.t. the proposed architectures for the control structure and the compensation methodology. As such, this paper proposes a theoretical and practical analysis of the two most used communication networks in the automotive domain, i.e., CAN and FlexRay. The theoretical analysis tackles the most important properties of these two networks, describing briefly their advantages and disadvantages. The practical analysis w.r.t. the time-varying delays induced by CAN and FlexRay communication networks on the control performances of a vehicle powertrain is performed using the TrueTime toolbox for Matlab. To do the comparative analysis, a predictive controller was designed and implemented, and the results illustrate that the obtained performances are not degraded even when time-varying delays are induced by both communication networks.

articleTitle: Changes in Engineering Education in the Transition to a Digital Society
abstract: The main trend at now is intellectualization and digitalization in all activity areas. First of all, in the transition to the Industry 4.0 concept, this relates to the creation of management systems, including in education. This is actual for engineering education, including the learning of specialists in the control and computer systems sphere. To create the information and communication infrastructure to digital economy, we need specialists who are able to create, develop and implement projects in the information and communication technologies. Requirements for a modern engineer imply his social responsibility, solicitous attitude to ecosystems and adherence to the sustainable development principles. The accelerating digitalization of modern society is increasing the demand for engineers with creative thinking, which leads to the new education philosophy development - Smart Education. The article discusses the requirements for the modern education system, the main of which is to motivate the student so that he learns to formulate the problem in a professional language and solve it using new intelligent technologies. A feature of the proposed method is the use in the educational system to solve real problems of such a digital environment, which is being introduced in the industry.

articleTitle: A Solution to Monitor Environmental Parameters in Industrial Areas
abstract: Monitoring the environmental parameters in active industrial areas where there are potential sources of pollution and, especially in the area of decommissioned or closed mining activities, is very important for the prevention of environmental accidents and for ensuring a suitable working environment for workers in one factory located in that area. In this paper, we propose a solution for monitoring the environmental parameters regarding air quality. After the data is acquired with the help of air quality sensors, they are sent using a LoRa type radio communication to a higher hierarchical level where it is processed and potential alerts for exceeding certain critical thresholds of the values can be issued. The whole autonomous system can be located in an industrial hall and in the test phase it has an autonomy of about eight hours. The monitoring equipment consists of sensors connected to LoRa modules.
