The communication between the sensors and these modules is done through a standard serial protocol. LoRa modules send data to a gateway system using a LoRaWAN protocol. This flexible structure represents a concept of hardware and software development that presents the possibility of being integrated into the national air quality monitoring network.

articleTitle: Software Solutions for Simulation, Monitoring and Data Acquisition in Wastewater Treatment Plants
abstract: This work approaches the design of software tools for a Wastewater Treatment Plant (WWTP) located in Făcăi, Romania, where the Distributed Control System/ Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (DCS/SCADA) solution consists in four specific levels. More precisely, the paper proposes software solutions for the emulation of the control system from the WWTP. Due to the complexity of a WWTP, the proposed solutions and tools are dedicated to two levels of DCS. The specific bioprocesses (e.g. the activated sludge process) are simulated and the results are compared with data provided by the data acquisition system. Also, a software solution for the monitoring of process data provided by various sensors is designed. The proposed software solutions will be useful in future research for the design of advanced control systems in the WWTP. The software models and tools are designed in Matlab/Simulink, but also in LabWindows CVI and other software environments.

articleTitle: Role of Asynchronous Motor Modelling in Driven Railway Wheelset Dynamical Simulation Model
abstract: In this paper, we proposed an improvement in existing Asynchronous Motor (ASM) Simulink model, considering the possibility of replacing the existing ASM mathematical model based on dq transformation, with another proposed one based on ABC natural coordinate frame. This idea leads us to consider a replacement of standardly implemented PI controllers in control of the torque delivered from the traction motor, with a non-linear model predictive control (MPC). We expect not only better control results, but also a better selection and use of directly measurable quantities in the detection of an unsuitable operating condition such as ripple in torque, loss of adhesion linked with loss of power decreased to select the best voltage vector to control the torque of the rail wear, etc.

articleTitle: Development of a Monitoring System on Environment and Human Health to Control a Smart Bike
abstract: Smart Mobility is one of the main directions of Smart City's transport system development. At the same time, along with the management intellectualization, the issue of the transition to cleaner, safer and more sustainable transport modes, such as a bicycle, is being resolved. Democracity and accessibility, cheapness and environmental friendliness, promoting a healthy lifestyle are the reasons for the growth of this transport type popularity throughout the world. The paper proposes one of the possible ways of developing bicycle transport in smart city, which allows to expand the its users number by reducing the requirements for the person physical fitness level. The proposed development represents the Smart Bike concept, which with the help of sensors monitors the condition of the environment and cyclist health, analyses indicators and, in critical situations, turns on the electric motor. This allows you to reduce the load on the cyclist, as well as battery consumption, which has a positive effect on the Smart City's ecology condition.

articleTitle: Improving the City’s Transport System Sustainability by Making an Justified Choice of the Optimal Infrastructure Solution
abstract: The article considers actual problem to ensuring the safety and sustainability of urban transport systems. The authors examined the existing positive global experience in both infrastructural and managerial decisions. To assess possible solutions at the stage of infrastructure design, the authors of the article developed the simulation models. On specific examples, the proposed method's effectiveness is shown. Case studies of cities of different sizes and layouts are implementation examples and possible uses proposed by the models. Studies have shown the effectiveness of the proposed solution at the stage of assessing infrastructure projects and choosing the best option for sustainable transport development. The proposed intelligent system is universal and can be applied in any city.
